chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Musa, from Zubyan ibn Hakim, from Musa al-Numayri, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I saw a guest with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). One day, the guest stood up to attend to one of the needs. He (peace be upon him) forbade him from doing that, and stood up himself to that particular need, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade making the guest serve.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on making a guest serve the host?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in hospitality, where the host’s duty is to serve the guest rather than burden them with chores. By tracing the prohibition back to the Prophet Muhammad, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a continuous prophetic tradition (*sunnah*) that elevates the guest’s status and reflects the host’s generosity and humility.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Musa, from Zubyan Bin Hakeym, from Musa Al Nameyri, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I saw a guest in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So he (the guest) stood up one day regarding one of the needs. So he<sup>asws</sup> forbade him from that, and stood up himself<sup>asws</sup> to that particular need, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from the guest serving’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Musa from Dhubyan ibn Hakim from Musa al-Numayriy from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following:

“I once saw a guest with abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who stood up one day to work for him (the Imam). He (the Imam) prohibited him. He (the Imam) himself stood up to do that work. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited making the guest to work. 5 ”
